title: When fine-tuning does not win
summary: A controlled comparison of LoRA, DoRA, and IA3 against zero-shot and five-shot math-reasoning baselines, followed by an audit and a same-pipeline rerun.
signal: No adapter beat the zero-shot baseline.
decision: Rerun every condition through one evaluation pipeline, and withdraw claims the evidence no longer supports.

study.problem: Does parameter-efficient fine-tuning improve multi-step math reasoning when training data and compute are constrained?
study.built: Built a training and evaluation harness for LoRA, DoRA, and IA3, with answer extraction and saved predictions. Then audited the original report and re-evaluated every adapter and baseline on the full GSM8K test split through one FP16 V100 pipeline, with bootstrap intervals and paired tests.
study.architecture: Adapters train Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct on 6,000 GSM8K examples for two epochs at seed 42, with a ten-epoch IA3 follow-up. Every condition is re-evaluated on the 1,319-question test split. Intervals resample questions 10,000 times, and exact McNemar tests use Holm correction across 15 comparisons.

decisions.title: Re-test the headline
decisions.body: Under the shared pipeline, zero-shot still has the highest accuracy, but it is not distinguishable from five-shot or two-epoch IA3. It is significantly ahead of LoRA, DoRA, and ten-epoch IA3.

decisions.title: Withdraw what doesn’t hold
decisions.body: The audit withdrew the original latency comparison, the overfitting explanation for ten-epoch IA3, and the category-level claims. Two of five headline claims changed under the rerun.

decisions.title: Preregister the next test
decisions.body: Phase 1 compared three LoRA training-target formats on the same questions, with a decision rule fixed in advance. None was distinguishable. Self-generated reasoning made answers longer without recovering accuracy.

results.label: Zero-shot accuracy
results.context: 979 of 1,319 GSM8K test questions; 95% CI 71.80–76.57%. Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct, FP16 V100 pipeline.

results.label: Best adapter: IA3, two epochs
results.context: 95% CI 69.67–74.45%; not distinguishable from zero-shot after Holm correction. DoRA 63.99%, LoRA 62.85%.

study.limitations: One model, one benchmark, and one training seed. The intervals reflect question sampling, not seed variability. Adapters share hyperparameters rather than per-method tuning, and the original baseline scores could not be reproduced within one percentage point. Phase 2 was canceled.
study.lesson: Rerunning your own experiment can change the conclusion. A good report says which claims survived.

chart.title: GSM8K test accuracy, one evaluation pipeline
chart.caption: Whiskers show 95% question-bootstrap intervals (10,000 resamples). 1,319 test questions, Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct, seed 42. Zero-shot, two-epoch IA3, and five-shot are not distinguishable by Holm-corrected paired tests.
